text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Even though income differences between men and women have narrowed, men still earn about 40 percent more than women in Austria. Only women employees in the civil service earn more than men there.
- Building society Wuestenrot wants to change from being a cooperative society to a public limited company. Wuestenrot want closer cooperation with Die Erste savings bank in the process.
- Credit protection agency KSV expects a new record high of up to 5,400 insolvencies this year.

- Klaus Muendl, director of Austria's central bank, expects Germany and France to keep the number of starting members in European Monetary Union low in order to avoid endangering the new single currency.
- Creditanstalt has most probably lost the race against Dutch ABN Amro bank to take over Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank. The result of the bid is to be presented today.
- Upper Austrian Raiffeisenlandesbank has taken over 49 percent of the province's Hypobank for 1.7 billion schillings.
- Susanne Riess-Passer, designated vice-chief of the far-right Freedom Party, has voiced ambitions for a role in the government.
- Austria's industry expects all to go well with the introduction of the single European currency.
- Luxury hosiery maker Wolford's turnover went up seven percent to 832 million schillings in the first half.
- Provincial chambers of economy have agreed on liberalising 24 professions by not requiring a licence for them anymore.
- Introduction of pegged exchange rates for European Monetary Union will bring profits for Austrian companies, the newspaper wrote.
